# Ignis Leadership

> Ignis Leadership helps lean commercial teams ignite governed human-AI systems to bid more, buy better and stay in control.

Ignis Leadership is the practice of Yorik Tisseau. He brings 17 years of experience across procurement, bid management and commercial leadership in energy, infrastructure and industrial markets, including senior roles at Bouygues, bp and RWE.

The central argument of the practice: AI should strengthen commercial judgement, not replace it. Ignis combines the organisation's process, evidence and capability with agents that prepare and coordinate work, while named people retain authority to direct, challenge, decide and approve.

## Who it is for

Lean commercial teams pursuing complex, high-value work and teams running tenders to award it, particularly in energy, infrastructure and industrial markets.

## Services

- Bid — Win work: bid management audit, human-AI process redesign, governed workflow design, operating model embed and team adoption.
- Tender — Buy well: tender management audit, human-AI process redesign, governed workflow design, operating model embed and team adoption.
- Engagement approach: audit the current process and capability, design and prove one bounded pilot, then extend the modular system across the lifecycle.

## Practical insights

- [RFP software or a bespoke agentic bid workflow?](https://www.ignisleadership.com/rfp-software-vs-agentic-bid-system): a buyer guide comparing established proposal-response software with a governed workflow designed around complex bid work, including when the right answer is both.
- [Why do unclear tenders produce incomparable bids?](https://www.ignisleadership.com/insights/why-do-unclear-tenders-produce-incomparable-bids): how unclear requirements, interfaces and evaluation methods cause suppliers to answer different versions of the tender.
- [When do tender clarifications become a second specification?](https://www.ignisleadership.com/insights/when-do-tender-clarifications-become-a-second-specification): when clarification answers alter scope, risk or evidence, the log becomes part of the controlled commercial baseline.
- [Is commercial work too judgement-heavy for AI agents?](https://www.ignisleadership.com/insights/is-commercial-work-too-judgement-heavy-for-ai-agents): why the work surrounding commercial decisions suits governed agents precisely because the decisions must remain human.

- [The proposal is becoming the easy part](https://www.ignisleadership.com/insights/the-proposal-is-becoming-the-easy-part): AI can produce more bid work, so the advantage moves to the decisions before and after it.

## Key concepts used on this site

- Governed human-AI system: a commercial operating model that combines the team's process, evidence and judgement with bounded agent tasks, named decision rights and human approval.
- Commercial memory: the usable record of what an organisation believed, why it believed it, what changed and who has authority to make the next commitment.
- Human accountability: agents prepare and coordinate while named people retain authority to direct, challenge, decide and approve.
- Modular adoption: start with one useful pilot, prove it under real conditions, then extend the system one capability at a time.

## Questions this site answers

### What can AI agents safely do in bids and tenders?

Agents can extract, reconcile, draft, check and coordinate bounded work using approved evidence and controls. People retain authority for strategy, relationships, price, risk, evaluation and every material commitment.

### How do you govern AI in bids and tenders?

Give agents approved evidence, bounded tasks and explicit controls. Keep named people responsible for strategy, evaluation, price, risk and final approval. Preserve the evidence and decision trail so outputs can be challenged and verified.

### Where should a bid or tender team start with agentic AI?

Start with one pressure point in live work. Audit the process, evidence, decisions and controls; prove one bounded capability; measure what changes; then scale only what the evidence supports.
